messages.author: 2b00a2adc2c6a30e
parts:
HI?
I used R/Qtl for genome-wide interval mapping in a F2 population and was
able to localise five loci on different chromosomes. I would like to
explore further the possibility of multiple genes on chromosome 11,
suggested by multiple peaks in the LOD curve. However, I am not sure how to
do this, ie how to perform a two-dimensional two-QTL scan of chromosome 11
only. I tried scanqtl but was unable to visualise the results. Also, should
the loci on the other chromosomes be added as covariates ?
Thanks for your help,
Marie

messages.author: f388084a0de67b60
messages.subject: Re:
parts:
I admit that we've not created sufficient tools to make
proper use of the scanqtl() results. It's on my list of
things to do.

I'd definitely recommend taking account of all inferred loci
when doing the 2d scan on chromosome 11. If you have fully
typed markers near the inferred QTLs, you can pull out the
genotype data for those and use them as additive covariates
in scantwo.

scantwo() has an argument "chr" that you can use to do the
2d scan on only selected chromosomes. Alternatively, you can
use subset(mycross, chr=11) to create a cross object with
just the chromosome 11 genotype data.

karl
